sha_binding.anchor_note: f2ee3eacb7760d25cda36fe2274ae5882ac73a38 is this branch's current head and the tree every receipt in this bundle was obtained at. It supersedes 762a97afea7fabe1d7e5b92901bb9580203fdd37, which was the anchor while that commit was the last one touching a non-proof path. It no longer is: five `main` resyncs have since brought non-proof changes into this branch — the readiness ledger, UTV2-1857 (.lane/lanes/governance.yml), UTV2-1858 (docs/mission/plan.md), UTV2-1843 (the app-root CLAUDE.md files and docs/03_product) and, most consequentially, UTV2-1859 (apps/smart-form/lib/form-utils.ts and its tests). UTV2-1859 arriving is why that mattered: it means the browser evidence below exercised the server change in this lane and the client change that unblocks it in one tree, which is the combined workflow and could not have been demonstrated at the earlier anchor.

browser_proof.status: PASS, with one bound stated explicitly rather than papered over
browser_proof.environment: Playwright against locally built code. The API child runs with every SUPABASE_* empty, UNIT_TALK_API_RUNTIME_MODE=fail_open and UNIT_TALK_QA_SEED_ENABLED=true, so apps/api/src/server.ts:303-321 falls back to createInMemoryRepositoryBundle(). No staging or production credential is present in this harness, by design — run-e2e-gate.mjs strips any SUPABASE|DATABASE_URL|SERVICE_ROLE key from the child environment. Persistence against a real database is proven separately under runtime_proof, and the two are deliberately not merged: that separation is why the staging database is not re-contaminated with UI fixtures.
browser_proof.why_this_evidence_exists: Server-side evidence is structurally blind to a client that refuses before issuing a request. UTV2-1859 proved that class exists on this exact path: a stale client mirror of the server rule this lane removed made the form refuse a player prop while every server test, the full unit suite and a green verify all passed. These runs are therefore the check that the request is actually issued and actually answered.

runs.command: NEXT_PUBLIC_SMART_FORM_QA_AUTH_BYPASS=1 npx playwright test -c apps/smart-form/playwright.config.ts apps/smart-form/e2e/phase-one.spec.ts --workers=1

runs.what_it_establishes: The no-event structured fallback completes end to end in a browser: real POST, HTTP 201, {lifecycleState: "validated", outboxEnqueued: false}, then the saved pick is read back out of the API via GET /api/picks?status=validated&limit=200 and asserted on — line -3.5, odds 105, metadata.distributionMode "track-only", metadata.eventId null, both canonical side participant ids — and GET /api/qa/pick-status/<pickId> confirms outboxId null and outboxStatus null. This is a saved pick verified after an un-intercepted submission, which is the evidence gap this run was asked to close.
runs.bound: The ticket is a TEAM spread. The player-prop variant is the next entry, and it could not be completed — see harness_limitation.

runs.name: un-intercepted player prop — the request is issued and the server answers for itself
runs.command: operator-run Playwright case driving NBA / manual fallback / no scheduled event / canonical player, with search/players fixtured and POST /api/submissions NOT intercepted
runs.result: the browser issued exactly one POST /api/submissions; the server answered 422 SMART_FORM_RELATIONSHIP_INVALID, "participant player-tatum is not canonical for sport NBA"
runs.what_it_establishes: Two things, both load-bearing and neither of them "the player prop saved". (1) The client no longer refuses: the request exists, with a truthful payload — metadata.distributionMode "track-only", participantResolution.resolution "canonical", eventId null on both the resolution and the metadata, and the resolved player carrying its teamId. Before UTV2-1859 this run issued zero requests. (2) The server does not trust the client: it re-resolved the asserted canonical player against its own reference data, found no such participant, and refused. That is validateSearchBackedPlayer failing closed, which is the property this lane most needs to keep — a client cannot talk the server into a canonical resolution the server cannot corroborate.
runs.what_it_does_not_establish: It does NOT show a player prop persisting, and the 422 is NOT evidence about this lane's rule. The refusal fires one step earlier than the rule under test, on participant existence rather than on team relationship. The persisted player-prop claim rests on the staging receipt under runtime_proof, where the participants rows actually exist.

harness_limitation.claim: A successful un-intercepted player prop is not reachable in the contained harness, and this was measured rather than inferred.
measured: GET /api/reference-data/search/players?sport=NBA&q=Tatum against the running contained API returns {"ok":true,"data":[]} — the in-memory repository holds no players. GET .../search/teams?sport=NBA&q=Celtics returns team:NBA:Celtics, so the probe itself is sound and the emptiness is specific to players.

packages/db/src/runtime-repositories.ts InMemoryReferenceDataRepository sets this.participants = options.participants ?? [], and createInMemoryRepositoryBundle() takes no arguments, so nothing can seed it.
Even if seeded, its searchPlayers maps teamId: null unconditionally — the exact field validateSearchBackedPlayer reads to establish the team relationship.
harness_limitation.why_not_repaired_here: The in-memory/Database parity gap is real and is worth closing, but closing it usefully requires seeding the bundle at its construction site, apps/api/src/server.ts, which is outside this lane's pinned file_scope_lock (packages/db/src/runtime-repositories.ts is inside it; server.ts is not, and a lock cannot be widened by an agent). Widening the harness is also not what this lane is for. Recorded here rather than filed, per the ratified filing threshold, and stated as a bound on the browser evidence rather than absorbed into it.
harness_limitation.consequence: No claim in this bundle rests on a browser-run player-prop persistence. The player-prop persistence claim is the staging receipt, and it is stated as such.

browser_proof.intercepted_test_is_request_coverage_onl: apps/smart-form/e2e/smart-form-submission.spec.ts:1366 routes **/api/submissions and fulfils it with a synthetic 201. It is request/payload coverage and nothing more: it asserts that exactly one POST is issued and that the captured payload is truthful. It asserts no HTTP response from the real server, no persisted row and no delivery state, because it never reaches the server. It is described that way here, in UTV2-1859's own bundle, and in the plan; any reading of it as persistence evidence is wrong.

scope.detail: All five declared paths are now changed. `apps/api/src/smart-form-validation.ts` was deliberately untouched through the first two commits — the browse defect was a data-layer bug and accommodating it in the validator would have loosened a real control. The edit that landed is the opposite shape: it replaces a blanket refusal with a server-side verification that is stricter than what the refusal protected. No path outside the pinned lock is touched.

limits: This lane changes where `getEventBrowse` and `searchBrowse` READ a player's team identity from — the provider `participants` observation edge instead of the empty canonical `teams` / `player_team_assignments` tables — and not what any published interface promises. No caller signature changes and no client change was required.

It seeds nothing and it deletes nothing. The canonical tables remain empty under parked provider ingestion, deliberately, and every production `participants` row is preserved. The proof-fixture repair is a read filter, never a DELETE; production data deletion is reserved decision 1 and is not proposed.

The fixture-exclusion predicate is the MARKER (`metadata.proofIssue` non-null), never 'has no team relationship'. In today's production data those two predicates select the same 26 rows, so the distinction is invisible in live data and is asserted against constructed rows instead — including a legitimate team-less player that is retained, and a `proofIssue` of JSON null that is retained.

The exclusion was applied only to `getEventBrowse` and `searchBrowse`. `handleSearchPlayers` / `handleSearchTeams` intersect UTV2-1854's already-filtered repository results with the event's participants, so an existing control already guarantees it there; that control is proven rather than duplicated.

`getEventBrowse` also reports `leagueId: null` from the same empty canonical maps. That is real and recorded, and it is NOT a submission blocker — `submission-service.ts` and `smart-form-validation.ts` never read it. It is out of scope here.

The staging receipt proves browse resolution, fixture exclusion, persistence of both pick shapes and non-delivery on a real database. It does not constitute the Milestone 1 pilot, which requires Griff's own browser against the deployed system.

The no-event admission is narrower than 'players are now allowed without an event'. A structured fallback player is admitted only when reference data itself resolves a team for that player AND that team is one of the two entered sides. A player with no resolvable team is still refused, and the refusal names the manual `canonical-coverage-gap` path — so honest provenance remains available and fabricated canonical provenance remains impossible.

The caller's `identity.teamId` is never a source of truth in this path; it is only ever compared against the relationship the server resolved. M5 is the control for that and it is the mutation most likely to be reintroduced by a later 'simplification'.

`picks.player_id` is left null for a Smart Form player prop while canonical `players` coverage is absent. That is the honest value — the submitting surface's identity is a participants.id and belongs in `participant_id`, which is where the row carries it. It is not a claim that player identity is unrecorded.

The browser evidence covers the un-intercepted TEAM path end to end, including the saved pick and its non-delivery. The un-intercepted PLAYER path is covered only as far as the request and the server's own refusal; its persistence claim comes from the staging receipt, not from a browser.

The contained Playwright harness cannot produce a successful canonical player prop, because its in-memory reference repository holds no players and hardcodes teamId: null. That is a harness parity gap, measured and recorded above, and it is not a statement about this lane's server rule.

None of the browser evidence is Milestone 1. Milestone 1 step 4 is Griff's own browser against the deployed system, and production is d3f69b804 — neither this lane nor UTV2-1859 is running there. Dispatching a deployment is reserved decision 8.
